AI-Native Organization Design
What organizations must redesign is not process. It is evidence.

When agents take on much of the execution, decision rights, information flow, authorization, acceptance, and retrospectives must be redesigned. This project is not about "how to use AI". It is about making organizational judgment testable.

Not more documents. Fewer context and better judgment for the next executor—human or agent.
The project is its own first instance.

01 / The Problem

The biggest risk in AI organizations: output that sounds right but cannot be falsified.

This is not a model-capability problem. It is an organizational-design problem. Three failure modes recur, and most "AI org" proposals happen to avoid them.

FAILURE MODE 01

Treating agent self-reports as evidence

"Done", "covered", "aligned"—these are claims, not evidence.

Constraint: evidence must be collectible in the real environment; the judge cannot be the producer.
FAILURE MODE 02

Conflating decision rights with capability

An agent that can call production is assumed to be allowed to change production.

Constraint: greater capability does not imply greater authority; they are two separate contracts.
FAILURE MODE 03

Substituting documents for judgment

Every extra index competes with the others; the larger the knowledge base, the less anyone knows which source to trust.

Constraint: large knowledge base, small working set; one authoritative source per key fact.
A design claim without a falsification condition is not knowledge—it is phrasing. — docs/proof.md
02 / Domain Model

Seven core concepts. Each has a boundary and one invariant.

The methodology transfers from harness engineering because both address the same structure: a fixed-capability executor whose output quality is determined by its environment. The difference: software constraints can be compiled; organizational constraints need human-judgeable evidence.

01

Decision right

who may say yes

Not execution capability, and not awareness.

Invariant: exactly one owner per class of consequential change, named to a specific person.
02

Capability

what can actually be done

Not what is permitted; capability can exceed or fall short of authority.

Invariant: capability and authority are registered separately; neither changes the other automatically.
03

Authority envelope

the contract of one authorization

Not a sentence like "grant permission X".

Invariant: six items—scope, time limit, quota, audit, revoker, rollback path. No rollback path, no authorization.
04

Proof contract

what counts as done, and who judges

Not activity, hours, tokens, or pages of output.

Invariant: evidence must be collectible in the real environment; the judge cannot be the producer.
05

Context flow

who must know what, and when

Not "everyone can see everything"—that is load, not context.

Invariant: one authoritative source per key fact; no manual maintenance in multiple places.
06

Judgment asset

a reusable judgment

Not meeting notes, chat logs, or raw traces.

Invariant: it must carry applicability and invalidation conditions, or it cannot enter the asset library.
07

Human attention

the unit of account

Not labor cost, and not automation rate.

Invariant: every efficiency claim must state where the saved attention went and what it bought.
03 / Evidence Levels

Every claim gets a level. Below the threshold, it cannot enter a decision.

Evidence is not an adjective. It is a set of judgeable conventions: level (L0–L3), status (five values), and closure (three values)—counted separately, never merged into a ratio.

L0 cannot decide A claim with no case and no boundary. Only a hypothesis awaiting validation.
L1 can inspire At least one real case with time, scale, and source; cannot support a decision alone.
L2 default threshold Falsification condition + explicit applicability boundary + at least one failure mode.
L3 can be generalized Run in a real organization, or controlled comparison, with counter-evidence recorded. This project has no L3 yet.

Five statuses (evidentiality)

  • Declared reachable: fields, exporter, and registration location are complete
  • Assumed reachable: the dependency is written down, never merged into declared
  • To verify: fields exist but have not been checked
  • Missing: no usable fields
  • Not established: evidence exists but the proposition is false

Forbidden as evidence

  • Output counts, coverage percentages without a denominator
  • Agent self-reports
  • A reviewer's "it feels clearer now"
  • Flows that only run in a demo environment

Six questions every design proposal must answer

01Which consequential changes were identified? Who owns each decision (by name)?
02What is the rollback path for each envelope? Who executes it?
03Who judges each constraint satisfied, and with what evidence?
04Which key fact has exactly one source? Where is it now?
05Under what conditions should this proposal be overturned?
06Where did the saved human attention go, and what did it buy?
04 / Change Card

One card carries one change from authorization to acceptance.

The change card is the single registration carrier for a consequential change. Reading only this card, the owner should be able to answer: approve or not, on what basis, which evidence is declared, which is assumed, whether the business result is closed, and which residual risks were accepted.

Eight gates (missing one blocks "authorized")

01The change class is registered, with a reason it is consequential
02The decision owner is named to a specific person, not a role placeholder
03Every executor's authority envelope has all six items
04The rollback path has a verifiable evidence source, not "should exist"
05Every control proposition has six fields and per-conjunct judgments
06Required input sets are registered; unregistered ones are listed as assumptions
07If the business proposition is unclosed, the owner has signed residual-risk acceptance
08If git is used as evidence, the pre-change status is clean and base_commit is recorded

Gate 7 cannot repair gates 3, 4, or 8. A missing envelope item, an unverifiable rollback path, or a skipped git pre-check can only be fixed—not waived by accepting residual risk.

Control propositions

"Does this text exist? Did the diff touch only the expected files?"—mechanically judgeable.

Five statuses + three closure values, covering every conjunct.

Business propositions

"Did this change actually make the next decision cheaper?"—the result the owner cares about.

Closed control propositions do not close the business proposition. If it remains open, the card cannot be marked "accepted".

Routing rule

Reversible, no external impact, no audit requirement: use the short form. Do not use a full card to create ceremony, and do not use the short form to bypass a consequential change. If unsure, ask: "Can this be rolled back easily?"

05 / Git as Evidence

Git is not an audit. It is a line-by-line register.

ADR-015 moved from proposed to accepted on 2026-11-13, based on its first complete use on a real repository change: all five conditions met, control propositions closed one by one.

Five conditions (missing one blocks "declared reachable")

  • A clean baseline commit before the change, with base_commit recorded
  • A change_commit after the change, with an empty git status --porcelain
  • The EPC cover contains collector, export time, object ID, file SHA-256 / blob_sha, and judge
  • Judgment sentences use only git diff base..change -- <paths> and git status --porcelain
  • The judge is not the author of the change

What it can prove

  • Content identity: commit_sha and blob_sha
  • Textual scope: which paths and lines changed
  • Whether the working tree was clean before and after
  • Whether the change can be reverted with git revert

What it cannot prove

  • Committer identity: author is set by local config
  • Correctness, tests, runtime, or production state
  • Independent review: there is no independent second party
  • Tamper resistance: local history can be amended, rebased, or force-pushed
commit_sha proves content identity, not correctness. — ADR-015 · boundary a

07 / Honest Limits

What this project is not—yet.

A methodology that claims to be falsifiable must apply the same ruler to itself. The following are facts, not disclaimers.

  • No real organizational cases. cases/ is empty; the ceiling is L2. There is no L3 and no generalizable rule.
  • No second party. The repository has only an owner and an agent; the judge is also the initiator. Independence is procedural, not audited.
  • No remote backup of the evidence archive. The private archive is local; remote fields (PR comments, branch protection, signed commits) must be registered separately if a remote is added.
  • The change card is a register, not evidence. A complete card does not make a change safe; it does not replace system exports, EPC archives, tickets, or release records.
  • Business propositions remain largely unclosed. Closed control propositions only show that the registration discipline is executable, not that the organization improved.
Self-reference risk

This repository is both the research output and the first instance of its own methodology. It can easily become internally coherent without external validation—which is exactly why falsification conditions are mandatory.

08 / Open Source

Open source.

Code is MIT; documentation and methodology are CC BY 4.0. The public repository uses a clean, fresh history with no local accounts or personal paths. The private repository remains the evidence archive.
